description.narrative:
Support to International Center for Asset Recovery (ICAR) for the implementation of the Operational Strategy 2025-2028 to prevent and fight corruption, money laundering and provide technical assistance and advice to recover stolen assets. Training and capacity building of national actors such as public prosecution, police, anti-corruption agencies, and financial intelligence units. Closer engagement with high-capacity jurisdictions and financial centers.
Impact: ICAR partner countries are more successful in deterring corruption and mobilizing resources for development and can rely on greater public trust in government because they are effective in recovering stollen assets.
Outcomes: 1) ICAR partner countries have anti-corruption chains that are better equipped to deliver sanctions and recover assets, 2) The International community develops stronger laws, international standards, and practices to make asset recovery more effective.
Partner countries: Ghana, Kosovo, Malawi, Moldova, Mozambique, Tanzania/Zanzibar, Zambia , (Ukraine), Ecuador, Peru, Fly-in-fly out: Bangladesh, Sao Tome e Principe, Colombia, Mauritius, Zimbabwe (Seychelles/FCDO)
In 2025, ICAR is currently supporting 19 countries in four regions, as follows:
Latin America (LatAm): Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico and Peru Europe: Kosovo, Moldova, Romania and Ukraine Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA): Ghana, Malawi, Mozambique, São Tomé e Principe, South Africa, Tanzania (including Zanzibar) and Zambia Asia: Bangladesh, Fiji and Sri Lanka
